stem.en: Ṛigveda 9.112.3 says: "I am a poet; my father is a physician, my mother is a grinder of corn". How does this challenge the idea that occupation was fixed by birth?

text.en: The speaker says that he has no family.
The speaker says that all three do the same work.
The speaker says that a king gave each person a job.
The speaker does different work from his father and his mother.

explanation.en: A son who is a poet, a father who is a physician and a mother who grinds corn are three occupations in one family. This is why the verse is often used as evidence that occupations were flexible in the early period.

hints.en: If occupation were fixed by birth, what would you expect of the son?
